key_insight: PlotGround introduces a way to benchmark plot digitization on real scientific figures paired with their source data, not just synthetic charts. This helps reveal how well current models recover quantitative values from the kinds of plots researchers actually publish.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of realistic benchmarks for plot digitization. Existing evaluations often rely on synthetic charts or limited chart types, making it hard to measure how accurately models can extract values from real scientific figures.
method: Builds an automated pipeline to construct plot digitization benchmarks from real scientific figures and their underlying source data.
Focuses on evaluating model performance on authentic scientific plots rather than simplified synthetic examples.
Supports broader assessment across chart types and real-world figure variability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more trustworthy way to evaluate and improve document understanding and figure parsing systems. It can lead to models that better support scientific reproducibility, data reuse, and literature mining.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of a scientific figure and its source data
Pipeline diagram showing benchmark construction steps
Bar chart comparing model accuracy on synthetic vs real figures
Icon set for scientific plots, data extraction, and evaluation
paper_title: PlotGround: Grounding Plot Digitization in Real Scientific Figures and Their Source Data
paper_authors: Yaohui Zhang, Binxu Li, Haoyi Duan, Jiacheng Miao, Yixin Wang
